_note: Live web-research enrichment for LITT-naive development candidates and key champions. Merged by build_account_cards.py into the research appendix and candidate rationale. Keyed by physician name.

Raymond F Sekula.title: J. Lawrence Pool Professor & Vice Chair of Neurological Surgery; Director of Minimally Invasive Brain Surgery, Columbia / NewYork-Presbyterian
Raymond F Sekula.current_institution: NewYork-Presbyterian / Columbia University Irving Medical Center
Raymond F Sekula.bio: Functional and skull-base neurosurgeon regarded as one of the world's foremost experts in microvascular decompression (MVD) and minimally invasive cranial-nerve surgery. Practice is dedicated to cranial neuralgias (trigeminal neuralgia, hemifacial spasm, glossopharyngeal neuralgia) and difficult skull-base tumors. 6,000+ surgeries including 2,500+ MVDs; co-editor of the textbook 'Microvascular Decompression Surgery'; previously Residency Program Director at Pittsburgh (UPMC).
research_focus: Endoscopic / keyhole minimally invasive cranial-nerve surgery

litt_candidacy.rationale: Entire clinical & research focus is vascular compression of cranial nerves (MVD) and skull-base tumor resection via open/endoscopic approaches. Does none of the ablation-amenable work that drives NeuroBlate adoption — no drug-resistant epilepsy/SEEG, intra-axial glioma, brain metastases, or radiation necrosis — so LITT is largely orthogonal to his practice.

papers.title: Which surgical technique has a superior clinical outcome in microvascular decompression? A systematic review and meta-analysis of transposition versus interposition for trigeminal neuralgia and hemifacial spasm
Decompression Surgery in Elderly Patients with Hemifacial Spasm Refractory to Botulinum Toxin
Microvascular decompression for developmental venous anomaly causing hemifacial spasm: illustrative case

training.fellowship: UPMC — minimally invasive brain/skull-base & microvascular decompression under Peter J. Jannetta
training.pedigree_note: UVA undergrad; Georgetown MD; internship, residency and fellowship all at Pittsburgh/UPMC as a direct trainee of MVD pioneer Peter Jannetta — the classic Pittsburgh functional/skull-base lineage. Professor & Residency Program Director at Pitt before joining Columbia in Feb 2022.
training.litt_exposure: His long-tenured home institution UPMC runs an established NeuroBlate LITT program (first in western PA, since 2015, ROSA-assisted, iMRI) — so his platform familiarity, if any, is Monteris NeuroBlate. But his subspecialty is MVD/skull-base, his residency predates LITT, and there is no evidence he personally performs LITT. Personal LITT practice not established.

Jeffrey N Bruce.title: Edgar M. Housepian Professor of Neurological Surgery Research; Vice-Chair, Neurological Surgery; Co-Director, Brain Tumor Center; Director of Skull Base Surgery — Columbia / NewYork-Presbyterian
Jeffrey N Bruce.current_institution: NewYork-Presbyterian / Columbia University Irving Medical Center
Jeffrey N Bruce.bio: Senior academic neuro-oncologic neurosurgeon and nationally recognized authority on complex brain and skull-base tumors — high-volume practice in gliomas, meningiomas, pituitary/craniopharyngioma, skull base, and pineal-region tumors (200+ pineal operations). Co-directs Columbia's Brain Tumor Center and directs the NIH-funded Bartoli Brain Tumor Research Laboratory. Best known for pioneering convection-enhanced delivery (CED) of chemotherapeutics for malignant glioma.
research_focus: Convection-enhanced delivery (CED) of chemotherapeutics for malignant glioma
Malignant glioma / GBM therapeutics & blood-brain-barrier drug delivery

litt_candidacy.rationale: Has exactly the population LITT targets (high volume of recurrent/deep gliomas plus stereotactic/minimally-invasive expertise), so technical adoption is plausible — but his research identity is built on convection-enhanced delivery, a competing local-therapy modality he has championed for decades, so LITT is neither his focus nor an obvious extension of his program.

papers.title: Convection-enhanced delivery of immunomodulatory therapy for high-grade glioma
Chronic convection-enhanced delivery of topotecan for patients with recurrent glioblastoma: a first-in-patient, single-centre, single-arm, phase 1b trial
Convection Enhanced Delivery of Topotecan for Gliomas: A Single-Center Experience
Regression of recurrent malignant gliomas with convection-enhanced delivery of topotecan

training.pedigree_note: UVA biochemistry; RWJ MD; NIH Surgical Neurology Branch fellowship; neurosurgery residency and entire faculty career at Columbia — a true Columbia lifer in the Housepian neuro-oncology lineage.
training.litt_house: Columbia/NYP — Monteris NeuroBlate (our installed program, McKhann); Medtronic Visualase also in-house
training.litt_platform: NeuroBlate (Monteris) — Columbia's installed program; Visualase also present
training.litt_exposure: Sits inside Columbia's NeuroBlate program (our installed base; McKhann-led) with Visualase also in-house. His 1985-90 residency predates LITT and his signature research is convection-enhanced delivery — a competing local therapy — not thermal ablation. No evidence he personally performs LITT; personal practice not established.

Brian Gill.title: Assistant Professor of Neurological Surgery, Columbia / NewYork-Presbyterian (Neurological Institute of New York); member, Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center
Brian Gill.current_institution: NewYork-Presbyterian / Columbia University Irving Medical Center
Brian Gill.bio: Neurosurgeon-scientist (MD PhD) who trained and was chief resident at Columbia, did a neurosurgical-oncology fellowship at Memorial Sloan Kettering, then returned to Columbia. Clinically focused on complex brain tumors; lab work on the peritumoral microenvironment and tumor-neuron interactions in glioma. Embedded in Columbia's McKhann/Schevon intracranial-EEG group and identified as the successor to McKhann's LITT practice; presents on LITT for brain-tumor management.
research_focus: LITT / laser ablation for brain tumors

litt_candidacy.rationale: Trained within Columbia's McKhann/Schevon epilepsy-SEEG group and named successor to the McKhann LITT practice; actively presents on LITT for brain-tumor management and runs SEEG-guided focal-epilepsy research — positioning him as a dual tumor-and-epilepsy ablation champion.

training.pedigree_note: Case Western undergrad; MD/PhD-track training and neurosurgery residency at Columbia (chief resident 2021), then a surgical neuro-oncology fellowship at MSK before returning to Columbia faculty — a homegrown Columbia product with an MSK oncology overlay.

National reputation in Chiari malformation, spinal dysraphism, pediatric brain/spinal tumors, and vascular malformations. A core surgeon in Columbia's Comprehensive/Pediatric Epilepsy Center — SEEG, resective epilepsy surgery, hemispherectomy, and MR-guided LITT for drug-resistant epilepsy.

Guy McKhann.title: Helene & Johannes Huth Professor & Vice Chair, Neurological Surgery; Co-Chief, Stereotactic/Functional & Brain Tumor Divisions, Columbia / NewYork-Presbyterian — incoming Chair of Neurosurgery, Emory University (effective Sept 14, 2026)
Guy McKhann.current_institution: Columbia / NewYork-Presbyterian (departing for Emory as Chair of Neurosurgery, Sept 2026)
Guy McKhann.bio: Nationally recognized epilepsy and brain-tumor neurosurgeon whose practice centers on awake/asleep brain mapping, glioma and metastasis surgery, epilepsy surgery, and minimally invasive stereotactic laser ablation (LITT). Directs Columbia's Epilepsy Neurophysiology Laboratory (human cortical neurophysiology, tumor-related epilepsy, NPH/Alzheimer's). The driver of Columbia's institutional LITT program — and departing for Emory as Chair of Neurosurgery in Sept 2026, which is the central risk to this account.
research_focus: LITT / MRgLITT for epilepsy and brain tumors
Glioma & brain-tumor surgery incl. tumor-related epilepsy

training.pedigree_note: Duke undergrad → Yale MD → University of Washington neurosurgery residency → additional training at London's Atkinson Morley's Hospital, a historic epilepsy-surgery center. An academic epilepsy/functional neurosurgeon-scientist lineage, not a device-specific LITT fellowship.
training.litt_house: Columbia/NYP — Monteris NeuroBlate (our installed program he built)
training.litt_platform: NeuroBlate (Monteris) — day-to-day; Visualase in the multicenter SLATE trial
training.litt_exposure: Substantial and hands-on. Personally performs stereotactic laser ablation for drug-resistant epilepsy and brain tumors and built Columbia's LITT program on Monteris NeuroBlate (ours).
